title: Predictive microbatch gating with KV hotness forecasting and slab-aware preemption
creator: Ayesha Kapoor
description: This ticket implements a predictive admission and preemption layer for microbatching that combines short-term KV cache hotness forecasting with GPU slab-aware preemption. Under sustained high QPS we see oscillatory admission decisions and repeated KV eviction/spill cycles that increase P95 latency and cause GPU memory fragmentation. Current fixed watermarks and simple headroom heuristics are insufficient for multi-tenant hotkey-driven traffic patterns. Goals: 1) reduce tail latency and eviction thrash, 2) keep GPU slab fragmentation low by coordinating microbatch admission with slab rebalancer, 3) provide deterministic degradation for lower-priority tenants during bursts.
acceptance_criteria: P95 latency on heavy-hotkey workloads reduced by >= 20% compared to current canary baseline (measured on staging harness)
KV eviction churn (evictions/sec) reduced by >= 35% for replicated-hotkey scenarios
GPU memory fragmentation metric (slab collision rate) reduced by >= 25%
Feature gated rollout: canary at 10% traffic then 50% with rollback metrics defined
Unit + integration tests covering forecast accuracy, probabilistic spill, and preemption ordering
Documentation for runtime config knobs and recommended defaults added to Console runbook
technical_notes: Overview: maintain per-tenant short window hotness model using lightweight Count-Min sketches + tiered sampling of request key fingerprints
Forecasting: compute 3 horizon EMAs (100ms, 1s, 10s) of hot-key scores and a fast quantile estimator for expected active-hotset size; use exponential smoothing to avoid reacting to single bursts

Admission decision: derive a dynamic waterline W_t = base_watermark * (1 + alpha * forecasted_hotset_density) where alpha is a tunable sensitivity; admission probability P_admit = sigmoid((headroom - estimated_kv_usage) / temp_scale)

Probabilistic spill: when forecast predicts sustained pressure, evict cold segments probabilistically based on LRU hotness delta to avoid synchronized thrash; spill threshold is a percentile over recent access ranks

GPU slab-aware preemption: coordinate with slab rebalancer service to identify low-impact slabs (tenant-owned low-usage shards) and preempt their microbatches ahead of evicting KV entries; preemption priority is tenant_score = SLA_weight / (1 + recent_tail_latency)
Backpressure signalging: emit deterministic backpressure tokens to frontend proxies with encoded reason codes (HOTSET_FORECAST_HIGH, SLAB_PREEMPT_REQUEST) for observability and rate limiting
Telemetry: new metrics: forecasted_hotset_size, admit_probability, probabilistic_spill_rate, slab_preempt_count, forecast_error_{horizon}, kv_eviction_churn
Safeguards: fallback to conservative fixed-watermark admission when forecast_error_exceeds threshold or if slab-rebalancer RPCs exceed latency budget
Rollout knobs: feature flag per-cluster, sensitivity alpha, temp_scale for sigmoid, min_admit_prob, max_spill_rate, preempt_threshold
Compatibility: works with current KV cache on-disk spill path and existing microbatch allocator; no schema changes to request payloads
